text.p: These are the headlines from selected Canadian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Floods, fire strike U.S. city: 50,000 flee Grand Forks, N.D., as blaze tears through downtown section.
- Israeli PM won't face charges in scandal: Suspicions linger over his role.
- Tax cut touchy topic: Voters question long-term effects on services, federal debt as they weigh parties' promises.
- Mental-evaluation process questioned: Judge overturns incompetency ruling.
- Hate fans flames in Northern Ireland churches: Relations between warring sides reach new low as U.K. election approaches.
- Busang saga threatens juniors: Fiasco over Bre-X find could crush dreams of Canadian miners with claims in Indonesia.
- Japan financial sector braces for Big Bang: Tokyo is proposing the largest shakeup the industry has ever seen. Already, the country's institutions are running scared.
- Reforms could bypass Japan's farm co-ops.
- Next NorTel chief to roam wider circuits: Incoming CEO John Roth says new services and boosting foreign sales are the best channels of growth for the telecom equipment maker.
- Internet shares surf to their own market wave.
- Thiessen pressured on C$: Bay Street wonders when or if central bank governor Gordon Thiessen will raise interest rates to counter chronic weakness in the currency.
- Brick to buy Algonquin as Molson-Miller deal ferments.
